o1.biggest_strength: It goes past the pilot data with timing advice: start sends mid-month so step 4 lands before close week. It also covers opt-out footers, reply handling and an A/B test.
o1.biggest_mistake: Step 1 asks for a 20-minute walkthrough, which is a heavier first ask than a cold, link-free email needs. The 'Last note from me' subject comes close to the closing-door urgency the brand avoids.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the step 1 ask smaller, such as a one-line reply, and show the total meetings expected if all 1,900 contacts are eventually triggered.

o2.biggest_strength: Very clear, honest reply-rate expectations. It says plainly that it does not multiply the segment and trigger effects, and gives per-100 and full-list projections that check out.
o2.biggest_mistake: There is no opt-out line or postal address for consent rules. Step 2 drifts into a product pitch ('Chargebee is built so...'), and step 4 opens with 'I have not heard back', which is filler.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add opt-out and compliance footers, cut the product pitch in step 2, and time sends around the month-end close.

reason: Both find the right segment, the pricing-change hook and the no-link rule. I'd take the first one because it also plans around my close week, handles opt-outs and replies, and gives me a test to run, though the second one sets expectations a little more clearly.
